raw_response:
This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability scores of the Mistralv0.2-Base model when fine-tuned on six distinct medical specialty domains—Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics—with each specialty represented by a group of six vertical bars corresponding to the same six specialties, indicating cross-specialty evaluation. The horizontal axis, labeled “Per-specialty terms,” categorizes the six medical specialties in left-to-right order, each with a cluster of six bars. The vertical axis, labeled “Negative log probability,” uses a linear scale ranging from -27 to -22, with tick marks at integer intervals, where higher (less negative) values indicate better performance. Each bar within a group is color-coded according to the legend: light blue for Mistralv0.2-Base (the base model), and six shades of orange and brown for the fine-tuned versions on Cardio (light orange), Gastro (medium orange), Infect (orange), Neuro (dark orange), Obstetrics (brown), and Pediatrics (dark brown). In each specialty group, the light blue bar (base model) is consistently the shortest (highest negative log probability, ~-26.5 to -27), while the bar corresponding to the same specialty as the group (e.g., the light orange bar in the Cardio group) is typically among the tallest (lowest negative log probability, ~-22.5 to -23.5), indicating improved performance after fine-tuning on that domain. The bars are not sorted by height within groups, and no bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or annotations beyond color coding.
